grades.1: Acute pain episode requiring pain treatment at home for pain exacerbation
grades.2: Acute pain episode requiring a visit to a medical facility (including Day Hospital) for any type of treatment for pain AND NOT requiring admission
grades.3: Acute pain episode requiring admission AND NO evidence of organ failure or any of the following complications: acute chest syndrome, respiratory distress, DVT, PE, stroke, splenic sequestration, or hyperhaemolysis
grades.4: Acute pain episode complicated with organ failure OR one of the following complications: acute chest syndrome, respiratory distress, DVT, PE, stroke, splenic sequestration, or hyperhaemolysis OR resulting in a life-threatening complication where life-supporting treatment is indicated, including mechanical ventilation, vasopressors, renal replacement therapy, or other life-supporting treatments
grades.5: Death in the setting of acute pain episode

grades.1: Incidental radiographic findings only (ischemia, hemorrhage, encephalomalacia, hemosiderosis) AND NO history of neurologic symptoms of stroke; exclude silent cerebral infarct
grades.2: Neurological symptoms during acute stroke (according to the NIHSS) AND symptoms resolved completely (TIA episode) OR mRS of 0 at discharge
grades.3: Neurological symptoms during acute stroke (according to the NIHSS) AND symptoms did not resolve completely (remained with at least one neurologic sequela as listed in NIHSS) AND mRS of 1-3 at discharge
grades.4: Neurological symptoms during acute stroke (according to the NIHSS) AND symptoms did not resolve completely (remained with at least one neurologic sequela as listed in NIHSS) AND mRS of 4-5 at discharge

grades.1: Splenic sequestration not requiring any treatment
grades.3: Splenic sequestration requiring treatment (i.e. erythrocyte transfusion, IV fluids, etc.) AND NO hemodynamic instability AND NOT requiring splenectomy
grades.4: Splenic sequestration AND hemodynamic instability OR requiring splenectomy

grades.1: Requiring none of the following: supplemental oxygen; simple or exchange erythrocyte transfusion; erythropoietin; BiPAP; any other supportive treatment other than antibiotics
grades.2: Requiring FiO2 > 21% to < 50% OR simple erythrocyte transfusion AND none of the following: BiPAP; high flow O2; exchange transfusion
grades.3: Requiring ≥ 50% FiO2 OR BiPAP OR high flow O2 OR exchange transfusion
grades.4: Requiring ≥ 50% FiO2 OR BiPAP OR high flow O2 OR exchange transfusion AND critical cardio-respiratory supportive interventions (e.g., vasoactive/vasopressor infusions, intubation, invasive mechanical ventilation)

grades.1: Priapism episode with or without the use of medications at home AND NOT requiring a visit to a medical facility
grades.2: Priapism episode requiring visit to a medical facility AND requiring treatment (e.g., medication) AND NO shunt
grades.3: Priapism episode requiring a visit to a medical facility AND requiring aspiration/irrigation AND NO shunt
grades.4: Priapism episode requiring a visit to a medical facility AND requiring shunt surgical intervention

grades.1: No unplanned visits to medical facilities for pain treatment within a 12-month period OR at least one of the following in the past 3 months: Pain and Hurt Score ≥ 81; PROMIS T-score ≤ 48 on pain interference; PROMIS T-score ≤ 41 on pain behavior
grades.2: 1-3 unplanned visits to medical facilities for pain treatment within a 12-month period OR at least one of the following in the past 3 months: Pain and Hurt Score 61-80; PROMIS T-score > 48 but ≤ 64 on pain interference; PROMIS T-score > 41 but ≤ 57 on pain behavior
grades.3: 4-10 unplanned visits to medical facilities for pain treatment within a 12-month period OR at least one of the following in the past 3 months: Pain and Hurt Score < 60; PROMIS T-score > 64 on pain interference; PROMIS T-score > 57 on pain behavior
grades.4: > 10 unplanned visits to medical facilities for pain treatment within a 12-month period OR at least two of the following in the past 3 months: Pain and Hurt Score < 60; PROMIS T-score > 64 on pain interference; PROMIS T-score > 57 on pain behavior

grades.1: eGFR 60-89 mL/min/1.73 m² AND albuminuria < 30 mg/g
grades.2: eGFR 45-59 mL/min/1.73 m² AND albuminuria < 30 mg/g OR eGFR ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m² AND albuminuria 30-300 mg/g
grades.3: eGFR 30-44 mL/min/1.73 m² AND albuminuria < 30 mg/g OR eGFR 45-59 mL/min/1.73 m² AND albuminuria 30-300 mg/g OR eGFR 60-89 mL/min/1.73 m² AND albuminuria > 300 mg/g
grades.4: eGFR 45-59 mL/min/1.73 m² AND albuminuria > 300 mg/g OR eGFR 30-44 mL/min/1.73 m² AND albuminuria > 30 mg/g OR eGFR 15-29 mL/min/1.73 m²
grades.5: eGFR < 15 mL/min/1.73 m² OR death due to CKD

grades.1: Stage 1 or Stage 2 SCR without vision loss
grades.2: Stage 3 SCR without vision loss OR Stage 1 or Stage 2 SCR with vision loss
grades.3: Stage 4 or Stage 5 SCR OR any Stage SCR with legal blindness
IQ evaluation 3 SD or more below mean

grades.1: Mild depressive symptoms OR PHQ-9 score 5-9 AND treatment not recommended
grades.2: Moderate depressive symptoms OR PHQ-9 score 10-14 AND limiting instrumental activities of daily living AND treatment recommended (e.g., pharmacologic intervention, behavioral therapy)
grades.3: Severe depressive symptoms OR PHQ-9 score 15-19 AND limiting activities of daily living AND treatment recommended (e.g., pharmacologic intervention, behavioral therapy)
grades.4: PHQ-9 score 20-27 OR life-threatening consequences (i.e., attempted suicide) OR threats of harm to self or others AND treatment recommended (e.g., pharmacologic intervention, behavioral therapy)
grades.5: Death due directly to depressive symptoms (e.g., suicide)

grades.1: Mild symptoms AND NO medical intervention indicated
grades.2: Symptomatic AND medical intervention sought (but NO supplemental oxygen) OR limiting instrumental activities of daily living (ADL) OR intermittent asthma requiring short-acting beta-agonists as needed AND NOT status asthmaticus
grades.3: Limiting self-care ADL OR supplemental oxygen indicated OR status asthmaticus
grades.4: Life-threatening respiratory or hemodynamic compromise (i.e., requiring intubation, pressors, invasive or non-invasive ventilation)

grades.1: Radiological findings of AVN AND NOT symptomatic
grades.2: Radiological findings of AVN AND/OR limiting instrumental activities of daily living AND NO intervention
grades.3: Radiological findings of AVN AND/OR limiting instrumental activities of daily living AND intervention with physical therapy, analgesics, bone remodeling agents OR invasive intervention with steroid injection or core decompression
grades.4: Radiological findings of AVN AND limiting instrumental activities of daily living AND invasive intervention with total joint replacement

grades.1: Intact skin with skin induration AND hyperpigmentation associated with pain/itching/burning/warmth, possibly edema
grades.2: Partial thickness skin loss AND less than 8 cm² AND minimal exudate AND periwound intact
grades.3: Full thickness skin loss involving subcutaneous tissue AND greater than 8 cm² AND < 50% wound bed with necrotic tissue AND moderate exudate AND periwound intact
grades.4: Full thickness skin loss involving damage or necrosis extending to the fascia AND greater than 8 cm² AND ≥ 50% wound bed with necrotic tissue AND heavy exudate, possibly malodorous AND periwound erythema, maceration + clinical signs of infection
